title: model loading - weights/shard failure breadcrumbs
content:
Quick breadcrumbs for the model loading failure we hit on prod-1 (dedicated):

Context:
- Model: customer-A/llama-like-7b-sharded (trained with HF sharded checkpoint: pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin + pytorch_model.bin.index.json)
- Serving runtime expects either a single consolidated checkpoint or HF-style sharded + index.json. We attempted to deploy as sharded.
- Failure surface: model fails to load during startup when downloading shard 3/8 from S3. Intermittent - sometimes starts (rare), mostly fails.

Symptoms observed (raw snippets):
- 2026-02-18T07:35:12Z - download started: s3://redwood-customer-a/checkpoints/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin
- 07:35:14Z - HTTP 206 Partial Content received then closed; file size on disk = 123,456,789 bytes (expected 123,987,654)
- torch.load error (during load_state_dict):
    EOFError: Ran out of input
    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 603, in load
      return _legacy_load(opened_file, map_location, pickle_module, **pickle_load_args)
- alternative run with safetensors: safetensors.errors.InvalidHeaderError: header too short
- runtime logs show: "Checksum mismatch for shard 00003 (expected SHA256: abcd..., actual: 1111...)"
- S3 server-side logs show several 5xxs for GET of the object around same timestamps (network flaps)

Commands I ran locally to reproduce /debug:
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-customer-a/checkpoints/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin ./ && sha256sum ./pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin
- curl -I -L https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-customer-a/checkpoints/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin
- python -c "import torch; torch.load('pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin', map_location='cpu')"  # immediate EOFError
- tried with safetensors loader for different model version (if HF saved as safetensors): python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; safe_open('pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin','rb')" -> InvalidHeaderError
- attempted partial-range download to validate server supports ranges: curl -r 0-1023 -o head.bin <url> -> succeeded (206)
- re-downloaded via aws s3 sync with --exact-timestamps; file size sometimes changes post-sync

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Corrupted object on S3 due to inconsistent upload/multipart failure. Some shards were uploaded with incomplete multipart parts -> intermittent reads (sometimes full, sometimes truncated).  -> Evidence: checksum mismatch + EOFError + occasional 5xxs in S3 logs.
2) Client-side premature close / insufficient retry logic in our downloader when fetching large shards (>1GB). We use aiohttp with default timeouts; need to ensure streaming writes and resume support. -> Evidence: HTTP 206 then closed; partial file sizes.
3) Index/manifest mismatch: index.json points to shards that are different size/ordering (e.g., training wrote 6 shards and index says 8) -> leads to wrong expectations during assembly. -> Evidence: some metadata in index.json doesn't match expected sizes for shard 5 in one run.
4) Checkpoint format mismatch: original trainer wrote safetensors, but filename .bin; our loader tried torch.load -> corruption or loader errors. -> Evidence: safetensors InvalidHeader when forced; but main error is EOF.

Immediate mitigation steps tried (results):
- Re-uploaded shard 00003 from trainer machine with verified sha256: did not fully fix; still some cluster nodes saw truncated downloads (suggests network edge or CDN issue).
- Switched serving runtime to download via signed URL pre-signed with S3 v4 and curl-based download rather than our aiohttp streaming client: reduced frequency of truncation but not eliminated on one EC2 az (us-west-2b).
- Added checksum validation in startup path: if sha256 mismatch -> fail fast and retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff. This reduces noisy partial loads but still sometimes fails all retries.
- For customers with strict uptime we rolled back to a smaller model variant (non-sharded) as a stopgap.

Data to collect next (actions / TODOs):
- [ ] Collect full server-side S3 access logs for the object (GET range requests, response codes) for timeframe 2026-02-18 07:00-08:00 UTC. -> ticketed to infra (JIRA-RENDER-128).
- [ ] Run a robust end-to-end multithreaded downloader test from each problematic AZ (us-west-2b) to validate network stability and transient errors. Use boto3 with retries and enable TransferConfig multipart_threshold=8MB, max_concurrency=10.
- [ ] Add a temporary debug flag in runtime to dump per-shard download byte counts and HTTP response headers (Content-Length, Accept-Ranges, x-amz-request-id).
- [ ] Compare index.json sizes vs actual shard sizes on S3 for all shards and verify manifest integrity via a signed manifest file containing sha256 sums.
- [ ] If repeated truncation, consider switching to ETag-based validation of multipart uploads (ensure completed multipart uploads committed) and consider forcing a re-upload using a single-part copy to avoid multipart edge cases.

Notes from chats / references:
- Maya: saw this with another customer last quarter; fixed by re-uploading with aws s3 cp (single part) instead of multipart upload from older CLI. (Slack thread: #ops-uploads, link in confluence page)
- Ethan: suggested adding HTTP range resume support in our streaming client and bumping timeouts; also to switch to HEAD+Range checks before full download to confirm full size.
- Related GH issue: serving-runtime#298 - broken-range-downloads on some hosts (linked PR attempted to add retries but not resume)

Quick reproduction recipe I keep using (for triage):
1) aws s3 cp s3://.../pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin ./ - tests if aws SDK can get the full object (usually succeeds or returns truncated file)
2) python -c "import hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(open('pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin','rb').read()).hexdigest())" -> compare with expected in manifest
3) if truncated: curl -v -L <presigned-url> --output shard.bin and inspect curl verbose logs for connection reset / early close

Open questions / things I don't fully understand yet:
- Why does a re-upload sometimes fix issue for some AZs but not others? Is there an S3 replication/accelerator/caching layer in front of our bucket that's returning stale or partial objects?
- Are multipart uploads from the trainer machine being finalized properly (complete-multipart-upload)? We should audit the trainer artifact upload pipeline.
- Do we need to change our canonical sharded checkpoint naming/manifest to include sha256 per-shard and expected Content-Length to catch these earlier?

Possible longer-term fixes / proposals:
- Mandate a signed manifest (sha256 + size) produced at training time and checked at serving before accepting a set of shards. Store manifest alongside shards as manifest.json.sha256.
- Add robust resumeable downloader in serving runtime with ETag/byte-range verification and parallel chunk retries. Use boto3 TransferManager for S3 downloads by default for large shards.
- Add a pre-deploy artifact verification step in the Dedicated deployment flow (validate all shards reachable & checksums match before traffic switch).
- Consider supporting safetensors explicitly and rejecting ambiguous filenames (i.e., if safetensors header != valid -> fail early and surface to customer).

Logs / useful outputs attached here (paste):
- Partial curl log:
  * Connected to s3.amazonaws.com (52.216.12.34) port 443 (#0)
  > GET /redwood-customer-a/checkpoints/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin HTTP/1.1
  > Range: bytes=0-
  < HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
  < Content-Length: 123456789
  < Content-Range: bytes 0-123456788/123987654
  < x-amz-request-id: ABCDEFGH
  <
  [downloaded 123,456,789 bytes in 4s (30.0 MB/s) but expected 123,987,654]

- Trace from runtime: (trimmed)
  2026-02-18T07:35:16.102Z WARN download shard 3 - got short read (bytes=123456789, expected=123987654)
  2026-02-18T07:35:16.103Z ERROR load model - EOFError loading tensor 'lm_head.weight'

If/when I get the S3 logs I will append them here. For now keep these notes as breadcrumbs for anyone continuing triage. If you pick this up: start by reproducing from us-west-2b and collecting HTTP headers for every GET (esp x-amz-request-id) so infra can correlate with S3 server logs.

Signed-off-by: Jordan
